changes.new: | **Ford circles** | Circle of radius $1/(2q^2)$ at $p/q$; tangent iff Farey neighbors [For38]. **Lifted-data map (Lean-verified, FF-3; shared library v23).** For lifted rosette data $(t_1,t_2,s,n_3)$ with $t_1,t_2\in\mathbb Z$, $s\in\mathbb Q$, $n_3\ge 1$ and a nonzero real amplitude $r$, the map $\Phi(t_1,t_2,s,n_3)=C(x)$ sends the record to the Ford circle at its Ford address $x=t_2s/n_3$. The phasor $r\,e^{i\pi a}$, with phase address $a=t_1s-x$, is real iff $a\in\mathbb Z$. On the lower-tooth shells $N=2,\dots,B+1$ ($t_1=t_2=1$), its real events with $s\in[0,N]$ are exactly $s=mN/(N-1)$, $0\le m\le N-1$, with addresses $m/(N-1)$; the deduplicated address set is the Farey set $F_B$, and consecutive members $a/b<c/d$ satisfy $bc-ad=1$. Along a finite address path, each edge is exactly one of tangent (determinant $\pm1$), stall (equal addresses) or break, and every tangent edge carries an exact rational kiss point lying on both circles. $\Phi$ is defined on lifted data, not on phasor values: at $N=3$, $s=0$ and $s=3$ give the same phasor and the addresses $0$ and $1$. Oriented or continuous Ford-circle arcs, a map from unlabelled phasor values or paths, and any dynamical correspondence are not defined; that comparison remains interpretive only. |
